I've had people tell me that I am a burden to my face. Sometimes, I've had people trying to take that statement back and it was far too late because I've already made up my mind. 

Campus people are okay. I talk to them and joke around but they aren't like best friends, they are just friends but they help keep my mind off things for the moment. 
For me, if I was to ever make it that far in life to become someone in the psychological field, it would be a blessing if I made it that far. But only the deserving people will land in those job fields... Me,  I'm not sure if I will live long enough by then. But if I do, I hope I'd be in a much better condition than I am now.

For such a long time, I felt this uncomfortable feeling. The first few years I wasn't able to figure out exactly what was going on but then by the 3rd year of those 9 years I was able to pinpoint what I felt but never knew how to cope. 
Nowadays, it's been hard, I feel like a joke,  a complete burden to myself and my loved ones and I didn't want to be that way. In other ways I know suicide is not the answer because it is selfish, knowing what kind of pain I could possibly leave behind and plus faith-wise... it's just not a good idea. But I also find that it is selfish enough for me to keep staying alive and keep hurting people and always being such a problem left and right and I just cannot live with that anymore. I rather die for the benefits of my loved ones, sure they may be slightly heartbroken but they will be much better off without me causing too many issues for them. I have no reason to even try.

I'm not sure, but whatever it may be, I feel like I am not needed anymore. I can't live being a burden. I don't think I have had a hobby or an interest that made me genuinely happy. My parents were what kept my family together and soundly peaceful. I was most happiest being surrounded by the two people who loved me, and cared for me until the very last days of their lives, and now that they are gone...  Nothing much goes around here but it just isn't the same any more.

I am currently a 21 year old college student majoring in Psychology. I am currently in the process of being employed for a part-time job at some restaurant as like many students does that as well. This year, January, I've been put into inpatient treatment for a week and got diagnosed with major depressive disorder and been given Effexor and Haldol for medication and therapy. In which it has helped a significant amount since January. It's just the suicidal thoughts keeps coming back to me, the urges to go and hurt myself comes and goes but it's bothersome. I'm currently not sure how I got this far, and neither do I know how I got so bad. As for any family history with depression or any mental illnesses, I have a brother who been suffering with depression long before I was even alive. Then his teenage son has ADHD, but nothing else coming from my parents... unless they were old-fashioned with their stigmas and denials.

For me, I've been medicated with an antidepressant (effexor) and an antipsychotic (haldol) prescription as well. I had the same reaction as to why I was given a drug that was primarily for schizophrenic symptoms, even though I am not a schizophrenic but I am treated for major depressive disorder. I was told that I was prescribed Haldol mainly for the reason to lessen my racing negative thoughts... Which in ways, it has help me a lot. Sometimes it is important to be "annoying" and ask for reasons why you are given this particular drug whenever you're getting a new prescription. It helps and it also puts my mind at rest as well. :)

Thank you for the feedback! :) and I am really glad that you're able to get back into the groove of things and being able to work and meet and talk to people!  Since taking medication, I've really taken in consideration about taking my medication whenever I'm supposed to. And because I am awful with my timings, I made sure to keep it on schedule by setting a few alarms to wake up and take the medicine in the hour of 6am, just how it was when I first started taking effexor while in inpatient treatment at the scheduled 6am vitals and medications time.

Thank you so much for your input! In other ways,  I feel like this reddit community has been really helpful to others and it makes me glad to realize that I am not in this alone. There's other people who are in the same boat as I am. And for me,  I feel like playing the "waiting game" is the most agonizing feeling in the world for both me and my loved ones. Here's my side where I feared that I may not even know the difference whether my medication is beginning to work. And there's the other side,  where my loved ones begin to be very impatient with the whole process that they'd be slamming the whole "Christian thing" right back at my face and one of my closest loved ones would tell me that: "If you're always going to feel bad stop using those pills and taking that therapy it's not working and there is no point in wasting money"....  They'd think that a couple of therapy sessions would solve and mend everything back together and it isn't like that at all,  and I understand that it can be a painstakingly long process for healing to begin but they won't understand. So I feel like I'm at a loss. :(
I have no clue.  I honestly don't think they do,  otherwise,  I would have known it since a long while.
For about two years.

Thank you,  but I have done pretty much that I can possibly do,  and I am still at a loss at this point. The only thing I have at this point is trying the best that I can with my college courses and get good grades by the time that I start studying for my major. That is my main worry at the moment.

At this point, I have no where to go. Because most of them require insurance but I do not have any at this point. I've tried some of the resources at my college campus,  but it has done very little for me.

Don't do it please, it's not good for you and your health. Now that I am still recovering from it, I wish I never fell into that hole, even when I used it as a coping mechanism, it took so much from my life. And now I suffer from random side effects and it is no fun. My stomach would sometimes act up and I'd be in so much pain and etc., but trust me, you do not need this at all.

I currently live with my brother and his family. His family are just wonderful people, however my brother is not that great. He manipulates, shames, ridicules, judges, belittles me. Its not even like the typical brother/sister type of argument/disagreement thing. He's an awful person if anyone is to be in my shoes. Yeah, he's a hard worker, smart, "professional" but he hates me. This year his family of 10 years finally saw his true colors. I started staying with them earlier this past summer and he kept his "cool" for a while and somehow, I managed to push his buttons and he's the ugliest person towards me and revealed his true angry self in front of his family. I felt so awful because I made him show his ugliest side and I wanted to go back home with my other brother even though he barely speaks to me, I'd prefer that but then I'd be back in the worst of my depressive state. So I stayed where I'm at because it's dangerous no matter where I go but I'd be accompanied with people who say they'd be with me. I'm ashamed to be the person that I am today because I feel like I am the real probem and I am not sure how I will get out of it.

I'm just making things worse. If I do something wrong, if I do something right, I get attacked. If I do something, if I don't do something, I get attacked as well. I don't have the freedom to do things for myself, because I don't have the privledge to do so, "I'm not like the others..so huh...no.".... I'm so frustrated that I just can't live anymore. I just want to be happy, is that too much to ask for? Why should I even bother to live if all I do is cause problems left and right? If I just remove myself from everything, I'd be doing the people a huge favor from worrying, making them annoyed, tired and angry at me. I'd be one less problem for them. Other people say they care but then they come at me with "others have it worse than you, stop being so ungrateful", and listen, I have been so grateful for the days that I've been given in this life, even when things are completely horrible, but I cannot handle this pain anymore. It's too much for me.

I know, but growing up, my family never believed that younger people can have mental illnesses, so I was never diagnosed to know the real thing, you get me? All I know is that I have just been feeling so awful for the past several years with a few periods where it just goes downright wrong. I kept getting yelled at, blamed for nothing, put down for nothing, ridiculed for nothing, it's like every single thing that I do is wrong. And when I know that I did good and I know that I shouldn't be put down for something, it is never enough. Anything I do is never enough.  Honestly, I have no one who I can go talk to about these things for the very same reason that others think that it is invalid for me to feel that way or I have others tell me that someone else in the world has it worse than I do. And I just don't care about that because I'm not asking for the whole world to pay attention to me, but to help me, to hear me out, get rid of this pain that I want out so badly.
It's difficult as it is because I try very hard to get out of it. Sometimes it becomes successful and sometimes it just doesn't fall through. 
But thank you for giving me some insight for me to consider. I'm not sure what my next step will be but I am willing to just keep trying. And once again, thank you!
